BiblicalUsage: Philosophia is philosophy, and Paul uses it once, as a warning. He tells the Colossians to beware lest any man spoil them through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe philosophy is not the enemy, but philosophy after the rudiments of the world is: any wisdom that does not start with Christ will end by spoiling me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
